title: Edge Deploy Garage: Hands-on Workshop Notes and Reference Snippets
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, hands-on set of notes and runnable snippets for a customer-facing workshop (aka the ‘Garage’ session) covering small-footprint, on-prem/edge LLM inference using Redwood Private with a hardware variety rack (NVIDIA T4, A10s, and a prototype ARM GPU node). Goal is a reproducible POC: get a canonical text-generation endpoint up, validate latency/cost, and hand off a checklist and minimal adapter shim for model variants and quantization profiles.

Audience and context:
- Audience: Platform engineers and ML infra leads at the customer; Redwood SEs run the session.
- Duration: 3.5 hours (setup & verification + breakout tuning + wrap).
- Assumption: customer has a small rack (2-4 GPUs), K8s cluster (1 control plane node), and access to their private control plane network.

Agenda (high level):
1) 15m intro + safety/risk notes
2) 45m guided setup: prebuilt container, runtime config, model pull
3) 60m smoke tests + KV cache and batching experiments
4) 40m quantization quick-run (int8/qat-ish) and cost/latency tradeoffs
5) 30m integration: routing policy & fallback to hosted variant
6) 20m wrap, next steps, and handoff checklist

Prework / prerequisites (customer and SE):
- K8s v1.26+ with NodePort or LoadBalancer support
- kubeconfig for cluster admin access
- Docker/OCI registry access (or use Redwood test registry)
- GPUs: at least one T4 or A10 accessible; optional ARM node for experimental branch
- Secrets for KMS if you want HSM tests (optional)
- Port range 9000-9100 open for test services

Quick repo pointers:
- git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-garage-workshop.git
- branches: main (stable), experimental/arm-optim (ARM kernel tweaks)

Minimal deploy steps (runnable):
1) Pull image and apply k8s manifest

# bash snippet
DOCKER_REG=ghcr.io/redwood-inference
IMAGE=${DOCKER_REG}/edge-runtime:20251101-canary
kubectl apply -f k8s/edge-runtime-deployment.yaml --record
kubectl set image deployment/edge-runtime edge-runtime=${IMAGE} -n redwood-edge

2) Create model artifact secret (example uses local registry creds)
# create secret
kubectl create secret docker-registry regcred --docker-server=ghcr.io --docker-username=${DOCKER_USER} --docker-password=${DOCKER_TOKEN} -n redwood-edge

3) Pull the quantized model (example uses S3-backed modelstore)
# CLI-style pseudo-command
redwoodctl model import --name tiny-falcon-q4 --uri s3://customer-models/tiny-falcon-q4.tar.gz --registry redwood-edge

Smoke test: curl generation endpoint
# wait for pod ready, then port-forward quick smoke test
kubectl port-forward svc/edge-runtime 9080:8080 -n redwood-edge &
curl -s -N "http://localhost:9080/v1/generate" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '
{
  "model": "tiny-falcon-q4",
  "input": "Summarize the deployment notes in one sentence.",
  "max_tokens": 64
}
'

Expected quick output fragment: plain text summary and generation latency printed in logs (~80-220ms per token on A10 for short prompts; higher for T4 depending on batch).

Key config knobs to show during workshop (live edits):
- runtime.batch.max_batch_size: 4/8/16
- runtime.cache.kv.enabled: true/false
- runtime.quant.profile: permissive|balanced|aggressive
- routing.policy.fallback: hosted|dedicated|local
- autoscale.cooldown_ms: 2000

Mini-experiments to run (with commands and expected observations):
A) Batching impact
- Change max_batch_size from 1 -> 8, run synthetic load yer 50 req/s with short prompts- Expect: throughput up, 95th latency spikes if cold KV cache; per-token cost drops ~15–40% depending on sequence length.

B) KV cache prefix warmup
- Warmup script: hit /v1/cache/warm with seed prompts to populate KV for common prefixes- Observe: 30–60% drop in p99 for repeated prompt families after warmup.

C) Quantization pass (fast path)
- Use the included quant script to produce a q4_0 style artifact (example in repo).
- Note: arm-optimized kernels may produce different perf; use experimental/arm-optim to test.

Sample quant snippet (pseudo):
# python quantize.py --input model.onnx --output model.q4 --mode fast --calib-samples 200

Adapter shim example (minimal Python adapter for fallback routing):
# file: adapters/fallback_adapter.py
import requests
import os

LOCAL = 'http://edge-runtime.svc.cluster.local:8080/v1/generate'
HOSTED = 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate'
def route_request(payload, prefer_local=True):
    try:
        if prefer_local:
            r = requests.post(LOCAL, json=payload, timeout=2.0)
            if r.status_code == 200:
                return r.json()
        # fallback to hosted with auth token (configured in env)
        r2 = requests.post(HOSTED, json=payload, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('RW_TOKEN')}"}, timeout=3.0)
        return r2.json()
    except Exception as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}

Notes: the adapter is intentionally tiny (for workshop/demo). In production, use the Redwood routing policy primitives to avoid client-side fallbacks.

Validation and metrics to capture during the workshop:
- Token/sec and tokens per GPU (via nvidia-smi + runtime metrics)
- 50th/95th/99th latencies for generation calls
- Cost approximation: tokens * unit_cost_for_profile (we use sample unit costs in the repo)
- Model fidelity check: run a small eval promptset (50 prompts) and compare response quality between float32 baseline and quantized variant (look for hallucination increase or truncation artifacts).

Troubleshooting quick hits (common issues and fixes):
- Pod OOM on load: reduce max_batch_size; increase limits.memory for container; try q4 artifact.
- GPU driver mismatch on ARM node: use experimental/arm-optim image; if unavailable, move workload to x86 node and test offline.
- Slow cold starts: enable persistent workers (replica count 1 warm pool) and KV prewarm endpoint.
- Unexpectedly high latency after quant: verify kernel selection log (env RW_LOG_KERNELS=1) and fallback to balanced quant profile.

Wrap and handoff checklist for customer success:
- [ ] Perms validated (kube + registry + s3)
- [ ] Model artifacts pulled and stored in customer modelstore
- [ ] KV cache warmup script added to cron or init job
- [ ] Routing policy defined for canary -> rollout -> full
- [ ] Basic observability dashboards copied (CPU/GPU, token rate, p95 latency)
- [ ] Follow-up ticket created: JIRA-SE-4217 (post-workshop tuning)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add a short guided section on HSM/KMS secret rotation for Private control plane (Priya to draft).
- Formalize the ARM perf numbers for the 2025 T4-equivalent boards (Samir).
- Create a small cheat-sheet for customers comparing quant profiles (Ava).

Appendix: quick smoke validation script (bash)
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for i in {1..10}; do
  ts=$(date +%s)
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:9080/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{"model": "tiny-falcon-q4", "input": "Test run $i", "max_tokens": 20}" >/tmp/gen.$i.out &
  sleep 0.2
done
wait
# quick parse
for f in /tmp/gen.*.out; do jq -r .choices[0].text $f || true; done | nl -ba

End of notes.

If running this workshop in the wild, favor short, repeatable experiments and keep one SE focused on metrics while another runs config changes. Capture a short Loom of the notable perf deltas for the knowledge base.
